title: Lighting of space habitats: Influence of color temperature on a crew's physical and mental health

findings.consequent: People's health, biological processes, psychological processes
findings.quote: Inadequate artificial lighting directly affects people's health and alters biological and psychological processes.

findings.consequent: Circadian rhythms, physical disorders, psychological disorders, health
findings.quote: The temperature of the light alters the circadian rhythms, causing physical and psychological disorders in the human body that affect health.

findings.consequent: Mental health, physical health, space psychology (especially in isolation)
findings.quote: we identify the need to incorporate variable wavelength lighting systems... on the influence of light on mental and physical health of humans and space psychology

findings.antecedent: Color temperature of a light source
findings.consequent: Psychology of human beings (especially when isolated in space)
findings.quote: The study places special emphasis on the color temperature of a light source, as it determines the influence on the psychology of human beings

findings.consequent: Biological processes, biological clock, hormone balance, health, well-being, alertness
findings.quote: health, well-being, and alertness are all influenced by light.
Human biorhythms (alertness, cortisol and melatonin) for a natural 24hour light/dark cycle

findings.antecedent: Inadequate lighting / Artificial light or light changes
findings.consequent: Discomfort, inconvenience, circadian rhythms, alertness, performance, sleep patterns
findings.quote: inadequate lighting creates discomfort or inconvenience, and artificial light or light changes alter our circadian rhythms influencing our alertness, performance, and sleep patterns.
light as being the biggest indicator, powered by daily ocular stimulus, which allows us to reset the circadian rhythm.

findings.antecedent: Constant artificial light (static light) at ISS
findings.consequent: Synchronization of hormones with light variation, hormonal rhythms, circadian rhythms
findings.quote: static" artificial light¹¹ alters both our hormonal and our circadian rhythms.
daytime light increases cortisol levels... and makes us more active.
At night high melatonin levels in the blood help us to sleep.

findings.consequent: Resetting circadian rhythm, nocturnal melatonin production
findings.quote: it has a direct influence on resetting the timing of the circadian rhythm by suppressing nocturnal melatonin production
Light is also used effectively as a cure¹⁸ for people suffering from seasonal affective disorder¹⁹ (SAD), shift-work or jet-lag

findings.consequent: Circadian rhythms, adaptation to new time zones/night shifts, alertness
findings.quote: Through the use of light and darkness, circadian rhythms can be changed in order to help people adapt to a new time zone
light has a strong influence on people's moods
a non-appropriate light makes us feel uncomfortable.

findings.antecedent: Lighting systems that do not mimic sunlight / Stable prolonged artificial lighting not following natural patterns
findings.consequent: Feelings of sadness, irritability, biological/physiological response
findings.quote: lighting systems that do not mimic sunlight... promotes feelings of sadness or irritability

findings.consequent: Sleep disorder, circadian rhythm disruption, mood, mental health, alertness, daydreaming
findings.quote: Human design issues that can affect crew psychology and effects of habitat design on behavior in long-duration confinement

findings.antecedent: Artificial lighting (constant color, indoor, closed space)
findings.consequent: Sense of confinement, disturbed connection with daily light cycle
findings.quote: This creates a sense of confinement and disturbs the connection with the daily cycle of light in nature.

findings.antecedent: Invariable white artificial light on ISS, 16 sunsets/day
findings.quote: This seems unnatural.
isolation and such close relationships with other human beings can create stress and interpersonal problems
interior design of space habitats improve the well-being of the crew.

findings.antecedent: Confinement in remote/isolated/high-risk environments (analogous to space)
findings.consequent: Undesirable symptoms, maladaptive behaviors, decreased performance, low morale, increased anxiety, sleep disturbances, fatigue, decreased productivity, hostility, interpersonal conflict
findings.quote: Experience has shown that workers who work in remote and isolated places... produce undesirable symptoms: maladaptive behaviors and a decrease in performance
The warm white light (3,000 K) facilitates relaxation and improves wellbeing
day-light (5,600 K) stimulates and activates the human body.
The circadian rhythm of cortisol begins with sunrise, reaching its peak at about 9:00 a.m.

findings.antecedent: Stress (physical, mental, emotional, spiritual, chemical, nutritional, electromagnetic or thermal)
findings.quote: this hormone is also produced when the body is subjected to any stress
space habitats not only have to control light in working hours to control melanopsin and cortisol and therefore alertness

findings.antecedent: Pleasant light environment (similar to natural light cycle)
findings.quote: also try to reduce stress... by generating a more pleasant light environment, similar to the natural light cycle of the sun.
The influence of diurnal light on the human body.

findings.consequent: Fatigue, low performance, phase-shifting circadian rhythm, nervous system activation
findings.quote: A long-duration short-wavelength light exposure is a potentially effective countermeasure for fatigue and low performance

findings.antecedent: Inappropriate utilization of short-wavelength light exposure
findings.consequent: Undesirable side effects on health and performance
findings.quote: to avoid undesirable side effects on health and performance caused by altering light environments beyond normative conditions

findings.antecedent: Dynamic lighting (variable amount and color of light, similar to natural light)
findings.quote: to simultaneously control the amount and color of light in a variable way... to regulate circadian system and create a pleasant atmosphere

findings.antecedent: Dynamic lighting (variable intensity based on activity/time)
findings.quote: Being able to vary the intensity at a given time... would help to prolong alertness and therefore performance.

findings.consequent: Sense of control over the habitat
findings.quote: using a choice of personal light, thus generating greater sense of control over the habitat.

findings.antecedent: Dynamic lighting (reproducing natural tonality, intensity, day-night cycles)
findings.quote: The aim here would be to reproduce those that benefit the crew.

findings.antecedent: Dynamic lighting (alternating color temperature 2600K-5600K, crew control)
findings.consequent: Crew members' sense of well-being, performance, motivation
findings.quote: Dynamic Lighting will help to improve the crew members' sense of well-being. If the crew can control their own space... they will increase their performance and motivation.
It has been proven³ that dynamic light benefits concentration and therefore work performance.

findings.antecedent: Dynamic lighting (varying lux and CCT over day)
findings.quote: Example of a natural rhythm of activity.

findings.antecedent: Dynamic lighting (cold/crisp light for morning, warm/reduced for lunch, cooler/whiter for afternoon, warm white for evening)
findings.consequent: Relaxation, countering drowsiness, readiness for night
findings.quote: The day starts with a cold and crisp light. For lunch, the light level is reduced and warm light promotes relaxation.

findings.antecedent: Higher Color Temperature (e.g., 6500K) and Vertical Illuminance (e.g., 300-400 lux)
findings.quote: Alertness benefit from Illuminants and Color Temperature: Comparison of Various Light Sources.

findings.antecedent: Crew control over lighting color (based on origin/culture) during resting hours
findings.consequent: Familiar environment, comfort zone, circadian efficacy
findings.quote: the crew could change the lighting color according to their city / culture of origin... thus creating a more familiar environment

findings.consequent: Circadian rhythms, hormones, body functions (sleep, body temperature, heart rate)
findings.quote: This internal clock regulates hormones and other essential body functions, necessary for sleep

findings.antecedent: Lighting that does not follow natural wavelength changes
findings.consequent: Circadian cycles, physical states, mental states
findings.quote: If we subject the members of a space crew to a type of lighting that does not follow the wavelength changes... their circadian cycles would be altered

findings.antecedent: Space architecture and environmental psychology (in habitat design)
findings.quote: The design of space habitats... must place special emphasis on space architecture and environmental psychology... in order to reduce disease and stress on the crew.
The dynamic changes in daylight have a positive influence on mood and stimulation

findings.antecedent: Smart lighting system (reproducing 24-hour daylight cycle wavelength changes, adapted to activities)
findings.quote: It would be appropriate to integrate a smart lighting system in aerospace habitats, which reproduce the wavelength changes found in the 24-hour daylight cycle

findings.antecedent: Light (as an 'intangible material' in habitat design)
findings.quote: This material is light, and it is vital to our rhythm of life.

limitations: Implicitly, the limitations of current static lighting systems in space habitats and the lack of implementation of dynamic lighting solutions that mimic natural light patterns.
